_provenance.note: Montana citation authorities. Montana's operative SNAP policy manual is DPHHS's Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program Policy Manual, cited by a numbered-section convention such as 'SNAP 304-1' (Categorical and Expanded Categorical Eligibility) or 'SNAP 801-1' (ABAWD Countable Months/Exemptions). Each section's own References line typically cites the parallel federal 7 CFR authority. This pack defines a SECOND citation family, 'arm', for Montana's Administrative Rules of Montana (ARM Title 37, chapter 76, the Food Stamp Program's administrative-rule codification this pack found via WebSearch corroboration, e.g. ARM 37.76.101), matching this roster's New Hampshire, Nebraska, Connecticut, Kentucky, Alabama, and Louisiana packs' multi-family pattern, though this pack notes it did not independently fetch the full text of any specific ARM 37.76.x rule beyond confirming the citation family's existence and rule-number format via WebSearch — flagged in freshness.json.

patterns.note: Montana DPHHS Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program Policy Manual, cited with the section number directly following the literal prefix 'SNAP' (matching DPHHS's own section-title convention, e.g. 'SNAP 304-1', 'SNAP 801-1', 'SNAP 1502-1'). This is the manual's own native citation format, unlike this roster's New Hampshire pack, which had to invent a disambiguating 'FSM' short prefix for a manual that does not use one internally.

Administrative Rules of Montana, Title 37 (Public Health and Human Services), Chapter 76 (Food Stamp Program). This pack confirmed the ARM 37.76.x citation family exists and covers the Food Stamp/SNAP program (e.g. ARM 37.76.101, ARM 37.76.111, ARM 37.76.122) via WebSearch corroboration of rules.mt.gov, but did NOT independently fetch the full text of any specific ARM 37.76.x rule — flagged in freshness.json as a citation-family confirmation without full-text verification.

Montana Code Annotated, Title 53 (Social Services and Institutions), Chapter 2 (Administration of Public Assistance), Part 9 (Food Stamp Program): 53-2-901 (Administration of food stamp program — rulemaking authority), 53-2-902 (Definitions), 53-2-903 (Employment and training program), 53-2-904 (Income and resource exclusions — FAIM participants). This pack directly fetched this part's section index via mca.legmt.gov and confirmed no standalone drug-felony-ban opt-out statute exists among these four sections — the drug-felony disqualification modifier is implemented through DPHHS administrative policy (SNAP 001/304-1/602-4), not through this statutory part.

mtsnap.note: Introduction — program overview, Montana Access Card naming, federal/state cooperative administration, congregate/meal-delivery prepared-meals provision
Gross and Net Income: Standards/Thrifty Food Plan — current FFY2026 GMI/NMI/ECE tables; drug-felony-disqualification supervision-compliance modifier text
Application Filing/Interview Process — apply.mt.gov, phone/mail/in-person filing, name+address+signature minimum filing standard
Non-Financial Requirements: Categorical and Expanded Categorical Eligibility — CE (TANF/Tribal TANF/SSI) vs ECE (200% FPG, non-cash) structure; drug-felony CE/ECE-exclusion condition
Resources Overview — resource limits $4,500 (elderly/disabled) / $3,000 (all other non-CE/non-ECE households); corrects the stale $2,750 figure several secondary sources repeat
Resources: Countable and Excluded Resources — alphabetical resource-exclusion catalog
Resources: Vehicles — federal-baseline exclusion (one vehicle, highest equity value), not a per-adult exclusion
Deductions (Earned, Standard, Dependent Care, Child Support) — Standard Deduction $209/$209/$209/$223/$261/$299 by household size
Deductions (Medical) — $35/month threshold, actual-expense-only, no flat shortcut
Shelter Deductions — SUA $799, LUA $267, OUA $116, Telephone $34; homeless standard shelter deduction and excess-shelter cap figures not published in this section (flagged gap)
Work Registration Disqualification — voluntary-quit/hour-reduction progressive penalty periods, distinct from the drug-felony-conviction disqualification
ABAWD Countable Months/Exemptions — current post-11/1/2025 exemption list; age-65 threshold explicitly stated as raised from 55 effective 11/01/2025
ABAWD Geographic Waiver — states directly: no approved ABAWD geographic waivers anywhere in Montana as of 11/01/2025
Recertification — 24 months (all-elderly/disabled no earned income), 12 months (Simplified Reporting), up to 24 months (change reporting, 12-month contact required)
